title: RICE+Signal Hedging: Dynamic Prioritization for Latency-Cost SLOs
creator: Maya Jensen
description: Problem: Standard RICE scoring (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort) does not capture running costs or latency SLO sensitivity that determine downstream economics of serving LLM features. For Redwood customers the effective value of an initiative depends on per-token cost, expected throughput latency targets, and whether Dedicated/Hosted routing is required. This ticket proposes RICE+Signal Hedging (RICE+) — a prioritization framework that augments classical RICE with dynamic penalties and multipliers derived from workload signals (latency sensitivity, token-econ, capacity constraints) so PMs can: 1) compare feature ideas across different economic regimes (high-throughput cheap tokens vs. latency-sensitive expensive tokens), 2) map initiative scores to OKRs and capacity plans, and 3) produce a ranked roadmap and a recommended deployment tier (hosted, dedicated, private).
problem_statement: PM teams lack a repeatable, cycle-ready rubric that blends product value (R,I,C) with operating economics (per-token cost, latency SLO tiers) and capacity constraints. Result: mis-prioritization of high-cost low-margin ingestion features and undue bias toward low-effort low-value work.
proposal_summary: Deliver a RICE+ scoring spreadsheet + dashboard integration that applies two adjustments: (A) LatencyPenalty — multiplicative penalty for initiatives that require P99 latency below a threshold; (B) CapacityMultiplier — scale benefit when initiative load maps to existing Dedicated capacity vs. new reserved capacity. A short reference formula: Score = (Reach * Impact * Confidence) / Effort * CapacityMultiplier / (1 + LatencyPenalty + CostPenalty).
scoring_explanation: Fields explained: Reach = monthly MAUs impacted estimate; Impact = qualitative 1-10 value to OKR; Confidence = 0-1; Effort = story points; LatencyPenalty = 0-1 penalty for latency SLO tightness (calc from P50/P95/P99 requirements); CostPenalty = 0-1 penalty that grows with expected per-token delta to baseline; CapacityMultiplier = 0.5-2 multiplier if request routing fits on existing Dedicated pools (>=1) or requires new reserved capacity (<1). The spreadsheet will include configurable curves for LatencyPenalty and CostPenalty to allow scenario sweeps.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype RICE+ model implemented as editable Google Sheet with scenario toggles for LatencyPenalty and CostPenalty
Integration of adjusted scores into the roadmap dashboard as an optional sort key
Playbook doc (Confluence) with step-by-step guidance for PMs: when to prefer CapacityMultiplier overrides, how to interpret score bands relative to OKRs
Case study: run model on top 20 backlog initiatives and validate rank changes against two recent planning cycles
Stakeholder review and sign-off from Eng leads and Finance on penalty curves and capacity assumptions
